set.servicesHeadline: Technical Services for Sustainable Construction Materials
set.servicesIntroduction: We support cement manufacturers, concrete producers and researchers through raw-material assessment, material characterisation, LC3 development, performance testing and technical consultancy. Our work connects laboratory findings with practical material and process decisions.
set.researchIntroduction: Our research examines local clays, supplementary cementitious materials and low-carbon cement and concrete. We study chemical and mineralogical properties of clays and SCMs include fly ash, slag, glass powder, and etc., hydration, strength, durability and also study thermo-mechanochemical activation to understand how material composition and processing affect performance.
set.eventsIntroduction: Explore our seminars, workshops, conferences and laboratory visits on LC3, cement chemistry and sustainable construction materials. These activities bring academics, researchers, stakeholders, government bodies and industry professionals together to share research and practical experience.
set.newsIntroduction: Follow our research progress, industry collaborations, laboratory developments, publications and outreach activities.

set.title: LC3 Technology
set.summary: Assessment of local raw materials, LC3 formulation and testing, with support for pilot and plant trials.

children.text: Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3) combines clinker, calcined clay, limestone and gypsum to reduce clinker use. We assess local clay suitability, optimise calcination and binder composition, and evaluate mortar and concrete performance. Our team’s experience includes national clay exploration, LC3 research and demonstration at NED UET, and technical work with Cherat Cement and Power Cement. We support laboratory development, staff training and the preparation and evaluation of pilot or plant trials, according to the agreed project scope.

methods: Clay surveys, sampling and raw-material screening.
Chemical, mineralogical and thermal characterisation using XRF, XRD and DTG–TGA.
Calcination trials, grinding and particle-size assessment.
Reactivity assessment using R3, and methylene blue value testing, interpreted alongside mineralogy and performance data.
Binder formulation, gypsum adjustment and mortar/concrete mix design optimization.
Hydration, strength and durability evaluation.
Technical assessment and monitoring of pilot or plant trials.
deliverables: Raw-material suitability and characterisation report.
Recommended calcination conditions and LC3 trial formulations.
Reactivity, hydration, strength and selected durability results.
Feasibility assessment and pilot/plant-trial plan where included in the scope.
Technical recommendations and staff training materials.

set.title: Material Characterisation
set.summary: Chemical, mineralogical, thermal and physical assessment of clays and supplementary cementitious materials.

children.text: We characterise clays, limestone, fly ash, cement and other candidate construction materials to assess their suitability for cementitious applications. Chemical composition, mineral phases, thermal behaviour and particle size are considered together with reactivity, hydration and performance results. This helps identify suitable materials, compare sources and select processing conditions. The test programme is tailored to the material and the client’s technical question, with specialist analyses coordinated through collaborating laboratories when required.

methods: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) for chemical composition.
X-ray diffraction (XRD) for mineral phase identification.
DTG–TGA and loss on ignition for thermal changes and mass loss.
FTIR and SEM–EDS for complementary structural and microstructural assessment.
Particle-size distribution and fineness assessment.
Isothermal calorimetry for hydration behaviour and R3 reactivity.
Methylene blue value testing for supplementary screening.
Interpretation of results alongside mortar/concrete performance.
deliverables: Characterisation report with test conditions, results and interpretation.
Chemical composition, mineralogical and thermal findings.
Particle-size, hydration and reactivity results for the agreed tests.
Comparison of candidate materials and suitability recommendations.
Recommendations for processing or further performance testing.

set.title: New Material Development
set.summary: Development and testing of low-carbon binders, blended cements and concrete using local and alternative materials.

children.text: We develop and evaluate cementitious materials through laboratory trials and performance testing. Our work includes LC3, activation of heterogeneous clays, fly ash, and other supplementary cementitious materials, recycled aggregate concrete and self-healing concrete. We examine how composition, processing and mix proportions affect hydration, strength and durability. Development begins with material assessment and proceeds through formulation and testing. Promising formulations can then be considered for demonstration or industrial validation, based on the results and project requirements.

methods: Screening of local and alternative raw materials.
Thermal and mechanochemical clay activation studies.
Binder formulation and mortar/concrete mix design.
Experimental comparisons and optimisation of material proportions.
Hydration, compressive, tensile and flexural testing.
Selected durability tests, including absorption, chloride-related testing and carbonation.
Research on elevated-temperature performance and self-healing behaviour.
Demonstration and trial planning for promising formulations.
deliverables: Material assessment and development plan.
Candidate formulations and processing conditions.
Laboratory specimens and comparative performance results.
Technical report identifying promising options and limitations.
Recommendations for further optimisation, demonstration or industrial validation.

set.title: Technological Support
set.summary: Technical consultancy, trial planning and training to support industrial adoption of sustainable construction materials.

children.text: We help industry partners translate laboratory findings into practical decisions on raw materials, processing and product development. Support includes LC3 feasibility assessment, technical review of clay calcination and grinding options, trial preparation, performance monitoring and staff training. Our experience includes cement-plant consultancy and coordination between researchers, plant teams and technology providers. Recommendations reflect the available evidence, plant conditions and agreed scope, with further trials proposed where additional validation is needed.

methods: Review of raw-material availability and test results.
Technical assessment of calcination, grinding and blending options.
Preliminary feasibility and conceptual engineering input.
Pilot/plant-trial planning, sampling and performance evaluation.
Quality-monitoring plans and technical documentation.
Staff training on LC3, material characterisation and testing.
Coordination with plant teams and specialist technology providers.
deliverables: Technical feasibility and implementation recommendations.
Trial protocol with sampling and testing requirements.
Evaluation report for the agreed trials.
Quality-monitoring guidance and technical procedures.
Training sessions and supporting materials.
Recommendations on the next steps for industrial validation.
